answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated work that independent counterparties verify and bond their own deposits against. Each accepted task adds a small, delayed reputation credit; a dispute or failed delivery burns the bond and removes credits across linked accounts. A sybil may create a hollow identity cheaply, but cannot cheaply manufacture many histories: it must lock capital, complete real tasks, and risk losing that capital. Shared funding or behavior can link accounts, while a copper-sized payment at the inlet still buys no instant trust.
